about: The authored features of the one continent (map version 4), laid on the owner's picture (order 73, D-153). Every x, y is a pixel of docs/design/m1/reference/owner-continent.webp (1536 x 1024). tools/m1/design-sketch.mjs reads this file with seats.tsv, builds the grid and draws the sketches.

transform.about: km = origin + scale * pixel, the same scale both ways: the picture's continent, islands and all, is centred in the game's frame with at least 200 km of sea on every side

latitude.about: degrees north at the frame's top and bottom, for the climate model (Ardan's degree is about 83 km)

edits.about: The few places where the grid departs from the picture's pixels, each listed for the owner in map-design.md

carveSea.name: the Cold Narrows
carveSea.why: the picture draws a channel some 30 km wide from the northern water to the sea; on the 10 km grid it is kept open two cells wide, so that Cold Bay is a bay of the sea and Aldmark's squadron can sail

carveSea.name: the Amber Strait
carveSea.why: the picture's winding channel across the neck of the south-east peninsula, cut clean two cells wide so that Great Amber is an island

carveSea.name: the Long Firth
carveSea.why: the picture's inlet under the Bleakfold, where the Brightwash and the Bleak Water meet the sea: kept open one cell wide

openWater.name: the Narrows of the Middle Sea
openWater.why: the picture's strait between the sea's two basins is narrower than a cell in places; it is kept open one cell wide so that the Middle Sea is one water

openWater.name: the Grey Water's arms
openWater.why: the picture's lake is drawn in three pools joined by necks narrower than a cell; they are kept one water

openWater.name: the Grey Water's foot
openWater.why: the same: the pool at the head of the Gullet

openWater.name: the Glenmere's eastern arm
openWater.why: the picture's lake runs on into its south-east corner by a neck narrower than a cell

addLand.name: Frostholm
addLand.why: the picture's islet off the Amber Capes is widened to the north-west into an island large enough for the giant halls and their tin

smallLakes.why: enclosed water of fewer cells than this that no name below claims is drawn as land: it is the picture's river water, which the rivers below carry, or a pond under the map's grain

dropLakes.why: blue shadow on the snow of the Trolness Fells, not water
blue shadow on the snow of the White Coast, not water
